definitions.explanation: The remaining base of a tree after it has been cut down.

examples.japanese: {切|き}り{株|かぶ}に{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: I sat on a tree stump.

examples.japanese: {森|もり}の{中|なか}にいくつもの{切|き}り{株|かぶ}が{残|のこ}っていた。
examples.english: Many tree stumps remained in the forest.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{切|き}り{株|かぶ}からキノコが{生|は}えていた。
examples.english: Mushrooms were growing from an old tree stump.

notes:
{切|き}り{株|かぶ} refers to the part of a tree left standing in the ground after the trunk has been cut down.

FORMS:
{切|き}り (from {切|き}る, to cut) + {株|かぶ} (stump, root stock). The {株|かぶ} component here means the base or root portion of a plant.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{株|かぶ}に{腰掛|こしか}ける: to sit on a stump
- {切|き}り{株|かぶ}を{抜|ぬ}く: to pull out a stump
- {古|ふる}い{切|き}り{株|かぶ}: an old stump
- {切|き}り{株|かぶ}から{芽|め}が{出|で}る: sprouts growing from a stump

CULTURAL NOTE:
Tree stumps appear frequently in Japanese folktales and children's stories, often as resting spots for forest animals. The Aesop-derived story 「{待|ま}ちぼうけ」 features a farmer who waits by a stump for another rabbit to crash into it.
